paragraphs: One-line judgment: Automotive Body and Glass Repairers are not about "a couple of taps and a coat of paint" but about linking vehicle damage assessment, sheet metal shaping, welding and cutting, grinding and painting, frame and dimensional alignment, and glass and accessory replacement into a checkable, measurable, reviewable repair process; people who only want to deliver the car as fast as possible and are unwilling to verify against process parameters and procedures are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you can read repair work orders and damage reports, judge the condition of the frame and panels by dimensions and symmetry, are willing to work to paint mixing ratios and process parameters and to work under ventilation and protective conditions, can complete degreasing and masking before painting, and stop and ask for guidance when structural parts, safety parts, or repair dimensions are unclear.

Conditions for pausing your investment: you have not yet completed one full assessment—shaping—grinding—painting—review process under any supervised conditions, or you can only describe your interest as "liking cars"; also do not treat course grades, one time helping a friend touch up paint, or being able to drive as proof that you can repair structural parts independently, weld and cut, or paint. Work involving welding and cutting, structural part repair, and painting must be carried out by organizations and personnel with the appropriate training and authorization following procedures; this page does not provide welding, painting, or field work instructions.

Education and authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists 49-3021.00 as Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0), and among respondents 42% think a high school diploma or equivalent is needed, 35% think a postsecondary certificate is needed, and 23% think less than a high school diploma is needed; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists the typical entry-level education as a high school diploma or equivalent and notes that most employers prefer to hire people who have completed a body or glass repair training program, and that industry certification is increasingly important. On the mainland China side, motor vehicle repair operations are subject to filing and classification management under the Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair, and body repair, auto detailing and trim, and auto glass installation and repair are special repair items; education, training, vendor and industry certification, an employer's internal authorization to work, and work authorization are different statuses and must be verified item by item according to employer, position, and location.

One line: this is an occupation that turns vehicle damage into measurable, reviewable repair results; the core is assessment, shaping, welding and cutting, grinding and painting, glass and accessory replacement, and quality review, with responsibility for repair dimensions, paint quality, and work safety, rather than an interest in cars or driving experience.

The work of Automotive Body and Glass Repairers falls into three categories: assessment and disassembly (reviewing damage reports and work orders, preparing or reviewing repair cost estimates and planning the work, removing interior trim, accessories, power window and seat operating equipment, and trim to reach the body and fenders, and identifying damaged panels and plastic types); sheet metal work and shaping (removing dents with dollies and hammers, removing small dents and pits from body metal with a pick hammer and punch, fastening the frame and parts to a hydraulic frame machine to straighten damaged areas, removing damaged sections with a metal cutting torch, pneumatic grinder, and wrenches and welding in replacement parts, repairing with polyester resin and hardener or fiberglass mat, and repairing plastic panels with a hot-air welding gun); and painting and assembly (filing, grinding, sanding, and leveling repaired surfaces with power and hand tools, masking and then spraying primer and topcoat, installing and fastening windows, vinyl tops, and metal trim, replacing damaged glass, adjusting or aligning headlights, wheels, and brake systems, and road-testing for review and cleaning the work area). All three categories presuppose stopping and escalating when structural parts, safety parts, or process parameters are unclear.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET 49-3021.00 Automotive Body and Related Repairers (page updated in 2026). The official duties are to repair and refinish automotive vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames, and they also involve windshields and window glass; there are 25 official tasks, covering leveling repaired surfaces with power and hand tools; inspecting repaired vehicles and road-testing them; installing replacement parts with welding equipment and grinding welds; spraying primer and topcoat; fastening parts to a hydraulic frame machine to straighten them; removing dents with dollies and hammers; reviewing damage reports and reviewing repair cost estimates; removing interior trim and accessories to reach the body; mixing resin and hardener; installing windows, tops, and trim; adjusting headlights, wheels, and brake systems; replacing damaged glass; repairing plastic panels; cleaning the work area; laying up fiberglass mat; and customizing modifications to customer requirements. Field boundaries: the summary page does not publish importance scores for tasks, and the task list describes the work of the group as a whole and does not mean every job performs all tasks. The details show 25 tasks in fact split into 22 Core and 3 Supplemental: surface leveling 88, completion inspection and road test 87, welding and installation 86, primer and topcoat 85; custom modification 68, custom glass cutouts 61, and roof cutting 60 are Supplemental. The original plastic task mentions softening with hot air or hot water before shaping, so it is not entirely equivalent to hot-air welding; Importance is not frequency or work authorization for all positions.

entries: Assessment and planning | Establish the extent of damage first | Review the damage report and work order, remove accessories to reach the body, identify damaged panels and materials, prepare or review the repair plan and labor and material costs, and mark the structural and safety parts that need review.

Sheet metal work and shaping | Make dimensions measurable | Remove dents with dollies and hammers and small dents and pits with a pick hammer and punch, fasten the frame and parts to a hydraulic frame machine and straighten to specified dimensions, and record the measurement results.

Welding and replacement | Verify the connection against process and real conditions | Officially this includes welding in replacements and grinding welds; the special operations training and assessment provisions effective 2026-06-01 define the work by catalog, and applicable tasks require specialized training and assessment and an operation certificate; an ordinary internal authorization or supervision does not replace the statutory conditions. The catalog was not fully verified this round, and the same certificate is not required of all body workers on the basis of the occupation name.

Grinding and painting | Verify the real process and applicable rules | Officially this includes grinding and masking, primer, and topcoat; mixing ratios and application records must be verified against real technical materials, Article 23 of the repair provisions covers safety education and safety procedures and Article 24 covers waste disposal in accordance with national requirements; the OSHA body hazards page is in fact a hazard and guidance link index, covering isocyanate asthma, solvents, dust, noise, and welding and cutting, and is not the full text of all current standards. The current EPA 6H introduction and the 2023 outreach summary cover applicable spray painting and paint stripping scope and exceptions, training, and paint controls, and do not imply the same permit or complete environmental conditions for all shops. This round did not obtain all PPE and ventilation parameters, fire and hazardous waste, and recovery procedures.
Glass and accessories | Get the fit right | Install and fasten windows, vinyl tops, and metal trim, replace damaged glass, and adjust or align headlights, wheels, and brake systems.

Review and records | Deliver according to the actual inspection division of labor | Officially this includes completion dimension and appearance inspection, road test, and cleaning the work area; Article 29 of the repair provisions requires repairing according to standards and publicly available vendor technical materials and not damaging emission systems such as OBD; Article 30 prohibits counterfeit and substandard parts, and requires recording purchase and use information, checking conformity certificates, and keeping the source. Article 31 applies intake, in-process, and completion inspections to level-two maintenance, assemblies, and whole-vehicle repair; Article 32 requires the corresponding release certificate to be issued by quality inspection personnel, with no delivery without a signature, and ordinary technicians or supervisors must not automatically sign on their behalf. Article 33 requires the electronic file to lawfully include the contract, work order, items, personnel, and settlement, and the listed repair additionally includes inspection and certificate copies; upload the genuine motor vehicle repair electronic health record.

Automotive Body and Glass Repairers handle body and frame repair, refinishing, and glass replacement and are responsible for repair dimensions, paint quality, and work safety; automotive glass installers focus on installing and repairing windshields and window glass; automotive service technicians and mechanics focus on diagnosing and repairing mechanical and electrical systems; sheet metal workers focus on forming and installing metal sheet; bus and truck mechanics and diesel engine specialists focus on heavy vehicle and engine repair; electric motor and power tool repairers focus on servicing motors and tools; motorcycle mechanics focus on motorcycle repair. Adjacent occupations share metal, mechanical, and painting knowledge, but the objects, deliverables, and responsibilities differ.
Measurable, reviewable repair results

Turn vehicle damage into measurable repair results, and leave a work order stating the extent of damage, the repair process and dimensions, the paint mixing ratio and application parameters, replaced parts, and open items, so that reviewers or the customer can accept the work.
Work orders, dimension, and process records

The objects are body panels, frames and structural parts, windows and windshields, vinyl tops and metal trim, and other components, along with welding and cutting equipment, hydraulic frame machines, sanding and painting equipment, measuring tools, and color matching systems; the basis is the vehicle manufacturer's repair technical information and labor time standards, the institution's process procedures and checklists, and the applicable welding and painting safety and environmental requirements.

Automotive Body and Glass Repairers (U.S. side O*NET 49-3021.00, Automotive Body and Related Repairers) repair and refinish motor vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames, and they also involve replacing and repairing windshields and window glass. The original official duties read "Repair and refinish automotive vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames."; there are 25 official tasks, focused on filing, grinding, sanding, and leveling repaired surfaces with power and hand tools; inspecting repaired vehicles for operating condition, completion, dimensional accuracy, and paint appearance and road-testing them; installing and welding replacement parts with wrenches and welding equipment and grinding welds; spraying primer and topcoat with a paint spray gun and power sander; determining the parts to repair or replace and the labor time per the supervisor's instructions; sanding areas to be painted and covering them with masking tape or paper to prevent paint contamination; fastening the frame and parts to a hydraulic frame machine to straighten damaged areas; removing dents with dollies and hammers; applying protective film and cleaning off adhesive; reviewing damage reports and reviewing repair cost estimates; filling small dents with plastic or solder; removing damaged sections with a metal cutting torch and pneumatic grinder and installing replacement parts; removing small dents and pits with a pick hammer and punch; removing interior trim, accessories, and trim to reach the body and fenders; mixing polyester resin and hardener; installing and fastening windows, vinyl tops, and metal trim; adjusting or aligning headlights, wheels, and brake systems; replacing damaged glass; identifying plastic types; repairing plastic panels with a hot-air welding gun; cleaning the work area; laying up fiberglass mat; determining custom modifications to customer requirements; and cutting openings in the body to install custom windows and cutting vinyl material. In the United States this occupation is in Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0); mainland China statistics are aggregated by industry category and do not list this occupation separately, so industry figures can only serve as a broad-scope comparison. This page does not constitute welding, cutting, painting, or field work instructions, and such work must be carried out by organizations and personnel with the appropriate training and authorization following procedures.
Assess—shape—weld—grind—paint—review

Assessment and planning → disassembly and shaping → welding or panel replacement → grinding and degreasing and masking → spraying to parameters → assembly and road-test review, or escalate per procedure.
Reviewable repair and painting records

The extent of damage and the repair plan, frame and dimensional measurement results, welding and replacement part records, paint mixing ratio and application parameters, glass and trim installation records, road test and acceptance conclusions, and a statement of open items.
The individual and the workshop supervisor (or quality inspection personnel)

Repair dimensions, process execution, and record accuracy are the individual's responsibility; authorization for structural part repair, welding and cutting, and painting is granted by organizations and personnel with the appropriate training and authorization following procedures, and when conditions are unclear work must stop and be escalated.
Education and preparation

O*NET lists 49-3021.00 as Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0), typically requiring a high school diploma or equivalent and providing from a few days to a year of on-the-job training; among the education levels published on the page, 42% is requiring a high school diploma or equivalent, 35% is requiring a postsecondary certificate, and 23% is requiring less than a high school diploma. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook notes that most employers prefer to hire people who have completed a body or glass repair training program and that industry certification is increasingly important, and O*NET also lists 5 hot technologies and 3 registered apprenticeship titles (automotive body repairer, service mechanic, and truck body builder). On the mainland China side, training is mainly for positions such as automotive operation and maintenance, automotive body repair, and sheet metal and painting, with specific requirements set by the employer.
Not interchangeable

Education, on-the-job training, industry and vendor certification, institutional authorization to work, special repair item filing, and position work authorization are different statuses: education does not bring institutional filing, and certification does not mean you can perform structural part repair, welding and cutting, or painting in any setting.

Check at least six items before starting: the occupational definition and the employer entity (O*NET 49-3021.00 is a U.S. definition, and on the mainland China side the position and the employer must be identified); education and training requirements; the employer's internal authorization to work and assessment; the scope of authorization for welding and cutting and for painting; paint environmental protection and waste disposal requirements; and the pay method (monthly salary, piece rate, or itemized settlement by labor time and material cost).
Occupational definition

The U.S. side is O*NET 49-3021.00 (Automotive Body and Related Repairers); on the mainland China side you must first identify whether the position belongs to a class one or class two auto repair enterprise, class three special repair (body repair, auto detailing and trim, or auto glass installation and repair), a 4S dealership body and paint shop, or an insurance claims and quick-repair chain, because different employers differ greatly in filing items, process management, parts traceability, and environmental requirements.
Education and major pathways

On the U.S. side O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0), typically requiring a high school diploma or equivalent and providing from a few days to a year of on-the-job training, and most employers prefer candidates who have completed body or glass repair training; on the mainland China side, training is mainly for positions such as automotive operation and maintenance, automotive body repair, and sheet metal and painting, with specific requirements set by the employer.
Authorization to work and work permits

On the mainland China side, motor vehicle repair operations are subject to filing and classification management under the Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair (Ministry of Transport Order No. 14 of 2023, fifth amendment): engaging in motor vehicle repair operations requires filing with the county-level competent transport department where the business is located; class one and class two auto repair operations must each be staffed with technical responsible personnel, quality inspection personnel, business reception personnel, and repair technicians engaged in mechanical repair, electrical, sheet metal, and paint work, and class three special repair is staffed with corresponding personnel by business item; body repair, auto detailing and trim, and auto glass installation and repair are special repair items. On the U.S. side it is determined by employer procedures and job authorization. Before starting, verify pre-job training, work permits, and review processes; this cannot be inferred directly from education or certification.
Equipment and site safety

Welding, cutting, grinding, and painting work must meet the applicable safety and environmental requirements (on the U.S. side, see OSHA body repair and painting requirements and EPA collision repair air toxics materials: ventilation, protection, and paint and solvent management; on the mainland China side, see the provisions of the Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair on safe production, waste disposal, parts traceability, and repair settlement); paint booths and mixing rooms must be used according to procedure. This page does not constitute welding, painting, or field work instructions.
Shifts and working hours

The work context shows that 66% work more than 40 hours per week, 53% face time pressure every day, and 54% consider the level of competition very high; common arrangements include overtime to meet delivery deadlines and peak-season scheduling. When comparing jobs, put the working-hours structure, the overtime and piece-rate arrangements, and whether settlement is itemized by labor time and material cost into the written terms.
Continuing training and review

New model materials (high-strength steel, aluminum, plastics, and composites) and painting processes update quickly (O*NET lists 11 software skills, 5 of which are marked as hot technologies, including collision damage estimating, spray mixing, and measurement software), requiring ongoing continuing training and maintenance of industry certifications; before starting, confirm the training arrangements, certification maintenance, and quality review mechanisms.

entries.answer: There are three core categories of tasks: reviewing damage reports and work orders, removing accessories to reach the body, identifying damaged panels and materials, and preparing or reviewing the repair plan; removing dents with dollies and hammers, handling small dents with a pick hammer and punch, fastening the frame and parts to a hydraulic frame machine to straighten them, removing damaged sections with cutting and welding equipment and installing replacement parts, and repairing with resin, fiberglass mat, or a hot-air welding gun; and leveling repaired surfaces with power and hand tools, masking and degreasing and then spraying primer and topcoat to ratio, installing windows, tops, and trim, replacing damaged glass, and adjusting headlights, wheels, and brake systems and road-testing for review. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 49-3021.00, whose official duties are to repair and refinish motor vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames.
entries.question: What do automotive body and glass repairers do every day?

entries.answer: Mainly fire and burns from welding and cutting, occupational health and environmental risks from grinding and painting, improper repair of structural and safety parts, substandard materials and parts with missing traceability, work beyond scope and unclear work authorization, and missing records and settlement disputes. The controls are ventilation and protection per procedure, working to process parameters, reviewing repair results by dimensions, and checking the parts source and keeping records. This page does not provide welding, painting, or field work instructions.
entries.question: What risks should I watch for in advance in this job?

entries.answer: The more explanatory signals are: being able to complete shaping, welding, grinding, and spraying to process and record honestly, reviewing repair results by dimensions and symmetry, and stopping and escalating when structural parts, safety parts, process parameters, or work authorization are unclear; "liking cars" alone cannot settle it. The Holland interest code is RC (Realistic + Conventional), and a consistent interest only indicates that the direction is close.
entries.question: How do I judge whether I am suited to being an automotive body and glass repairer?

entries.answer: AI and automation can change damage estimating and quotation support, damage measurement and dimensional comparison, spray mixing and color matching, and labor time and parts ledgers and settlement compilation; but there is no official evidence that they will replace on-site damage determination, frame and dimensional measurement, welding and structural part repair, and spray application and quality release responsibility as a whole. The official materials also do not give an automation substitution rate or a job disappearance year for this occupation.
entries.question: Which tasks will AI change?

entries.answer: Determining the extent of damage, frame and dimensional measurement, decisions on repairing structural and safety parts, welding and cutting process execution, paint mixing and spray parameters, glass and accessory installation quality, and road test and quality release conclusions must all be undertaken by the individual according to institutional procedures; tool output must first be marked as reference and can only enter the formal work order and settlement after on-site measurement and process verification.
entries.question: Which steps must retain manual review?

entries.answer: U.S. side: O*NET lists 49-3021.00 as Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0), and the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists the typical entry-level education as a high school diploma or equivalent and notes that most employers prefer to hire people who have completed a body or glass repair training program, with industry certification increasingly important; certification is used to demonstrate specific abilities but is not a statutory work permit. Mainland China side: motor vehicle repair operations are subject to filing and classification management under the Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair, and class one and class two operations must be staffed with technical responsible personnel, quality inspection personnel, and repair technicians engaged in sheet metal and paint work, and body repair, auto detailing and trim, and auto glass installation and repair are special repair items. Education, training, certification, unit filing, and position authorization cannot substitute for one another.
entries.question: What qualifications must be verified to enter this occupation?

entries.answer: Yes. The O*NET work context shows that 95% need to use their hands to handle tools and equipment continuously or almost continuously, 52% bend or twist continuously or almost continuously, 52% stand more than half the time, 50% kneel, squat, bend, or crawl more than half the time, and 47% walk or run more than half the time; the ability list includes manual and finger dexterity, arm-hand steadiness, trunk strength, near vision, and color discrimination. It also requires material and process understanding and dimensional measurement and record-keeping ability.
entries.question: Does this job require a lot of physical strength?

entries.answer: The work context shows that 66% work more than 40 hours per week, 53% face time pressure every day, 100% are exposed to contaminants every day, 84% are exposed to noise every day, 81% are exposed to hazardous conditions every day, and 88% wear routine protective equipment every day. Common arrangements include overtime to meet delivery deadlines and peak-season scheduling; when comparing jobs, put the working-hours structure, the overtime and piece-rate arrangements, ventilation and protection conditions, and whether settlement is itemized by labor time and material cost into the written terms.

subject.summary: Automotive Body and Glass Repairers assess vehicle damage and repair and refinish motor vehicle bodies, straighten frames, and replace windshields and window glass, and the core is shaping to process, welding, grinding and painting, and checking dimensions. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 49-3021.00 (Automotive Body and Related Repairers), in Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0); mainland China statistics are aggregated by industry category and do not list this occupation separately, and motor vehicle repair operations are subject to filing and classification management under the Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair; industry figures do not cover overtime pay or piece-rate commissions.
